SSE stream for coreference analysis of a chapter (ANAL-005).

Resolves pronoun references to character names, flags ambiguous
pronouns, tracks character mentions, and scores referential clarity.

**SSE Event Stream:**

1. ``"result"`` event with the full coreference analysis
   (resolutions, character_mentions, clarity_score, summary).
2. ``"done"`` event (``is_final=True``).
3. ``data: [DONE]`` termination signal.

On failure, a ``"error"`` event (``is_final=True``) precedes the
``[DONE]`` sentinel.

SSE stream for character-voice analysis of a novel's chapters (ANAL-008).

Profiles each speaking character's voice (deterministic metrics + LLM
qualitative judgement), writes the result to each character's KB
``speech.voice_analysis``, and streams per-character results.

**SSE Event Stream:**

1. ``"progress"`` event (character count / status).
2. One ``"result"`` event per profiled character (carrying that
   character's ``CharacterVoiceResult``).
3. ``"done"`` event (``is_final=True``).
4. ``data: [DONE]`` termination signal.

On failure, an ``"error"`` event (``is_final=True``) precedes the
``[DONE]`` sentinel.

SSE stream for checking a chapter's dialogue against voice profiles.

**SSE Event Stream:**

1. ``"progress"`` event with pipeline status.
2. One ``"result"`` event per speaking character.
3. ``"done"`` event (``is_final=True``).
4. ``data: [DONE]`` termination signal.

On failure, an ``"error"`` event (``is_final=True``) precedes the
``[DONE]`` sentinel.

SSE stream for longitudinal character-voice drift analysis (ANAL-009).

For each character with a stored ANAL-008 profile (``voice_metrics``) who
speaks in ≥1 selected chapter, computes the per-chapter match trend +
adjacent-chapter jumps, runs the governed ``voice_drift`` agent (1 call
per character), and streams per-character results. Read-only — nothing is
persisted.

**SSE Event Stream:**

1. ``"progress"`` event (character/chapter count / status).
2. One ``"character_result"`` event per analysable character (carrying
   that character's trend + jumps + overall score/band + agent
   classification), OR a ``"no_profile"`` event per character that cannot
   be analysed (RULE-11 graceful skip).
3. ``"done"`` event (``is_final=True``).
4. ``data: [DONE]`` termination signal.

On failure, an ``"error"`` event (``is_final=True``) precedes the
``[DONE]`` sentinel.

SSE stream for author-voice analysis of a novel's chapters (ANAL-007).

Profiles the narrator's voice (deterministic metrics + LLM qualitative
judgement over the full prose), writes the resulting
:class:`AuthorVoiceProfile` to ``ProjectSettings.author_voice``, and
streams the assembled profile.

**SSE Event Stream:**

1. ``"progress"`` event (chapter count / status; soft warning when below
   the 3-chapter minimum).
2. One ``"result"`` event carrying the assembled
   :class:`AuthorVoiceProfile` (single profile per novel — author voice
   is the narrator's voice, not per-character).
3. ``"done"`` event (``is_final=True``).
4. ``data: [DONE]`` termination signal.

On failure, an ``"error"`` event (``is_final=True``) precedes the
``[DONE]`` sentinel.

SSE stream for longitudinal author-voice drift analysis (ANAL-009 Phase 2B).

Compares the narrator's per-chapter metrics (voice-generic + author-
specific) against the stored :class:`AuthorVoiceProfile`'s metric group,
computes the per-chapter match trend + adjacent-chapter jumps, runs the
governed ``author_voice_drift`` agent (1 call), and streams the single
narrator result. Read-only — nothing is persisted.

**SSE Event Stream:**

1. ``"progress"`` event (chapter count / status).
2. One ``"result"`` event carrying the narrator's trend + jumps + overall
   score/band + agent classification, OR a ``"no_profile"`` event when the
   narrator cannot be analysed (no stored profile / missing metric blocks
   / no chapter with prose — RULE-11 graceful).
3. ``"done"`` event (``is_final=True``).
4. ``data: [DONE]`` termination signal.

On failure, an ``"error"`` event (``is_final=True``) precedes the
``[DONE]`` sentinel.

AuthorVoiceDriftResult.title: AuthorVoiceDriftResult
AuthorVoiceDriftResult.description:
Longitudinal author-voice drift result (display-only — never persisted).

Carries the deterministic per-chapter match trend (signal i, with author-

adjacent-chapter jump points (signal iii) + the aggregate match score +
the agent's qualitative :class:`VoiceDriftResult` classification. Singular
(one narrator per novel — contrast Phase 1's per-character list).

Attributes:
    novel_id: The novel analysed (str for JSON safety).
    trend: The per-chapter match trend (signal i) — one
        :class:`TrendPoint` per chapter with non-empty prose. The
        always-visible sparkline / heatmap row.
    jumps: The adjacent-chapter jump points (signal iii) — localise where
        drift began. Empty when no metric shifted beyond the threshold.
    overall_match_score: The mean of the per-chapter ``match_subscore``
        values in ``trend`` (a single [0, 100] summary of the whole
        trend). ``None`` when ``trend`` is empty.
    overall_band: The drift-facing severity label for
        ``overall_match_score`` (``"stable"`` / ``"minor"`` /
        ``"moderate"`` / ``"major"``), derived from ``band_for_score``
        (identical thresholds to WRITE-010 + Phase 1, ADR-073 D4).
        ``None`` when ``overall_match_score`` is ``None``.
    drift: The agent's qualitative longitudinal classification
        (:class:`VoiceDriftResult` — ``drift_type``, ``confidence``,
        ``longitudinal_reasons``, ``per_chapter_notes``,
        ``suggested_attention``). The OUTPUT shape is reused from Phase 1
        (ADR-073 D3 locked shape applied to the narrator trend).

AuthorVoiceProfile.title: AuthorVoiceProfile
AuthorVoiceProfile.description:
Machine-derived author-voice profile (ANAL-007 / ADR-074).

Persisted as ``ProjectSettings.author_voice`` JSONB. Novel-scoped.
Mirrors the ADR-055 descriptive/metric structure (deterministic metrics +
LLM qualitative descriptors), REUSING the voice-generic
:class:`~narrare_core.schemas.voice.VoiceAnalysis` /
:class:`~narrare_core.schemas.voice.VoiceMetrics` and ADDING
author-specific prose-level metrics.

Descriptive group (rendered into ``{{author_voice}}`` by
:func:`render_author_voice_for_generation`):
    - ``voice_analysis`` descriptive fields (formality, vocabulary_level,
      sentence_profile, emotional_range, cultural_regional_markers,
      voice_examples).
    - ``author_examples``.

Metric group (comparison ONLY — NEVER rendered into generation):
    - ``voice_analysis.voice_metrics`` (voice-generic metrics).
    - ``author_metrics`` (author-specific prose-level metrics).

The descriptive/metric boundary is enforced at the consumer contract
(:func:`render_author_voice_for_generation`), not at the data model — the
same place ADR-055 enforces it for character voice (``get_speech_data``).
The profile itself deliberately carries BOTH groups so the future Phase 2B
author-drift checker can read the metric group via the repository contract.

Attributes:
    voice_analysis: Voice-generic descriptive block (also carries the
        voice-generic ``voice_metrics`` sub-block).
    author_examples: Author-specific curated representative prose passages
        (the agent's ``author_examples``).
    author_metrics: Author-specific prose-level metrics. Comparison-only.
    updated_at: ISO timestamp of the last profile build (freshness signal).
    is_fresh: Freshness flag (mirrors character-voice ``profiles/_freshness``).

EpubOptions.title: EpubOptions
EpubOptions.description:
EPUB-specific options (pandoc).

Libertinus Serif (the bundled OFL font — the same files PDF uses, D3) is
embedded **unconditionally** via pandoc ``--epub-embed-font``
(regular/italic/bold/bolditalic). There is intentionally NO
``embed_fonts`` flag: PDF embeds the font structurally (Typst compiles it
in — no toggle), and EPUB matches that one-font-policy structure so there is
a single, footgun-free embedding model across both binary formats. A v1
toggle would only reintroduce the silent-fallback failure mode the
no-silent-fallback principle exists to prevent (D7). Markdown is plain text
and carries no font.

``isbn`` / ``description`` (IO-001 follow-up) are **request-level,
user-optional** EPUB metadata: there is no DB storage for them in v1, so
the export request is their only source. The runner merges them into
:class:`narrare_core.export.contracts.ManuscriptMetadata` (request wins
over the DB-absent defaults) and the EPUB renderer emits them as
``dc:identifier`` (``urn:isbn:`` URN) / ``dc:description``. EPUB-only
(D7 precedent): the PDF/MD renderers ignore both fields.

JumpPoint.title: JumpPoint
JumpPoint.description:
An adjacent-chapter jump (signal iii output).

Produced by :func:`narrare_core.analysis.voice_drift_scoring.detect_adjacent_jumps`
for each pair of consecutive chapters where at least one metric shifted
beyond the threshold. Jump points localise *where* drift began.

Attributes:
    from_chapter_id: The earlier chapter of the pair.
    to_chapter_id: The later chapter of the pair.
    jumped_metrics: Which metric(s) shifted beyond the threshold between
        the two chapters (e.g. ``["avg_sentence_length"]``). At least one
        entry — empty jumps are never emitted.
    magnitude: Normalized ``[0, 1]`` magnitude of the jump — the mean of
        the jumped metrics' distances. Higher = sharper jump.

ReadabilityMetrics.title: ReadabilityMetrics
ReadabilityMetrics.description:
Formula-based readability scores (deterministic per ADR-021).

        ``0.0`` when no metric is comparable). Derived from
        :func:`metric_delta_subscore` semantics — ``(1 - mean_distance) * 100``.

        ``"moderate"`` | ``"major"``) — derived from :func:`band_for_score`
        via :data:`narrare_core.analysis.voice_drift_scoring._VOICE_CHECK_BAND_TO_DRIFT_LABEL`

``CharacterVoiceRequest`` — novel-scoped endpoint). The body carries
optional filters:

Attributes:
    character_id: Scope the analysis to a single character by their
        stored profile ``character_id`` (the KB entity UUID string).
        ``None`` means "analyse every profiled character" (the default).
    chapter_ids: Specific chapter ids to analyse (UUID strings). ``None``
        or an empty list means "analyse every chapter in the novel"
        (the service resolves the full chapter list via the novel
        repository). Mirrors ``CharacterVoiceRequest.chapter_ids``.

VoiceDriftResult.title: VoiceDriftResult
VoiceDriftResult.description:
Structured longitudinal drift classification for one character.

The locked output shape Frontend + Backend consume (ADR-073 Decision 3).
A single flat object — the agent classifies one character per call.

Attributes:
    drift_type: Exactly one of ``"evolution"`` (intentional arc-driven
        change), ``"context"`` (chapter-context-driven variation), or
        ``"inconsistency"`` (unexplained drift). The single best-fitting
        label — no hedging.
    confidence: Float ``0.0``-``1.0`` capturing how confident the
        classification is given the trend + jumps + profile.
    longitudinal_reasons: Concrete observations that justify the
        classification, each tied to a specific trend feature (a declining
        metric, a jump at a specific chapter, an oscillation). May be empty
        only when ``confidence`` is ``0.0`` (the empty-trend convention).
    per_chapter_notes: Sparse per-chapter commentary — only chapters with
        something concrete to say appear. Empty when no chapter warrants
        individual commentary.
    suggested_attention: Chapter ids (drawn from the supplied trend) most
        worth the author's review. Empty when the voice is stable.
